title: Government-issued PDFs and letters lock blind and low-vision people out of benefits, forms and public records
affected_user: Blind, low-vision and print-disabled people who must read or fill government documents (benefits letters, tax and voting forms, court and school notices); secondarily the agency staff who must remediate those documents
job_to_be_done: Read a notice or complete a form from a public agency independently, on time, with a screen reader
current_process: Agencies publish scanned or untagged PDFs and mail paper letters; the user runs OCR locally, asks a sighted person to read it, requests an 'alternative format' from a special team, or gives up and phones the agency; agencies remediate documents by hand with Acrobat or outsource tagging
what_fails: Scanned PDFs contain no selectable text so screen readers read nothing; untagged PDFs have no reading order or form-field labels so fields are announced as unlabeled edit boxes; alternative-format requests arrive late or not at all, so deadlines are missed
failure_frequency: High for anyone with regular agency contact. In the UK DWP High Court case the claimant received 21 inaccessible or delayed letters versus 2 timely accessible ones between 2020 and March 2023 (leighday.co.uk). In the US, only ~37% of agencies' top-viewed public electronic documents were fully Section 508 conformant in FY2025 and 27% of agencies did not test documents at all (section508.gov).
cost_of_failure: Missed benefit deadlines and appeals, loss of independence/privacy (having a third party read medical or financial letters), compensation and litigation for agencies (DWP paid compensation after the 2023 ruling; DOJ Title II enforcement against a county election website). Exact dollar figures per user: unknown.
existing_workaround: Phone OCR apps and local OCR; asking family; agency alternative-formats teams; avoiding PDF forms entirely and preferring web forms (reported in a published study); legal action via RNIB/Leigh Day
who_pays_today: Agencies pay remediation vendors and staff time for manual PDF tagging and alternative-format production; disability charities fund litigation; the affected person pays in time and lost benefits

sources.note: FY2025 governmentwide assessment: 37% of top-viewed public electronic documents fully conformant; 1.1.1 Non-text Content is the most common document defect (self-reported data).
Average accessibility conformance score 1.96/5 across 212 responding agencies/components; ~half do not routinely test ICT for conformance.
Press summary: nearly a quarter of agencies failed to test at least one of their top digital products.
High Court declared DWP in breach of the Equality Act; claimant got 21 inaccessible/delayed letters vs 2 accessible ones; scanned PDFs without selectable text were the failure mode.
DWP agreed to pay compensation and improve services after the ruling.
2026 article quoting an r/Blind commenter that scanned PDFs lacking OCR leave screen readers with no text to read.
Study finding blind users frequently find PDF forms very hard to fill with screen readers (meaningless labels, broken reading order) and many avoid PDF forms altogether.
NFB comment to NIST: 43 states had voting forms that were not fully accessible (older filing).

firsthand_evidence: A blind UK benefits claimant, backed by RNIB, documented receiving 21 letters he could not read (scanned PDFs with no selectable text, or paper) against only two timely accessible ones over three years; weeks after winning in the High Court he was still receiving inaccessible letters. An r/Blind commenter quoted in a June 2026 article described scanned PDFs without OCR as giving a screen reader literally nothing to read.
key_unknowns: How many US state/local agencies produce accessible documents (no equivalent of the Section 508 assessment exists for them); per-document cost agencies currently pay vendors for tagging; whether AI-assisted tagging output is accepted as conformant by auditors (PDF/UA, Matterhorn checks)
technical_unlock: Vision-language models can now infer reading order, headings, table structure and form-field semantics from rendered pages, which was the manual part of PDF tagging; open-source PDF libraries can write tag trees and form-field names; validation against PDF/UA is automatable (veraPDF). A solo developer can build a document-remediation pipeline and a user-side 'make this readable now' tool without institutional access.
why_now: DOJ Title II web/document rule (now due April 2027 for entities over 50k population, April 2028 for smaller ones, after a one-year extension effective April 20, 2026) explicitly covers documents on public-entity sites; FY2025 Section 508 assessment published March 2026 made the document gap measurable; EU EAA in force June 2025
existing_solutions: Adobe Acrobat auto-tag, CommonLook, Equidox, Allyant/CommonLook, axes4, PDFix, veraPDF (validation), agency alternative-formats teams, overlay vendors (not endorsed by DOJ)

title: Small public entities (towns, school and special districts) must bring every web page and app to WCAG 2.1 AA with no accessibility staff, vendor-built sites and no exemption
affected_user: Clerks, IT generalists, communications staff and contracted web vendors at small municipalities, school districts, libraries, water/fire/transit districts; the disabled residents who cannot use their sites today
job_to_be_done: Know what on their site fails, fix it (or get the vendor to), and prove compliance before the DOJ Title II deadline, within a part-time staff budget
current_process: Rely on the CMS vendor's claims, run a free automated checker, buy an overlay widget, or hire an audit firm; remediation of a large site is described by vendors as routinely taking 12-18 months
what_fails: Entities have no in-house expertise to interpret audit output; vendor-built sites and third-party embeds (payment portals, agenda systems, GIS maps) fail but the entity still bears liability; overlays do not satisfy DOJ; automated tools miss most WCAG criteria yet 95.9% of top home pages fail even the automated checks
failure_frequency: Near-universal: 95.9% of the top 1,000,000 home pages have detectable WCAG 2 failures with an average of 56.1 errors per page in the 2026 WebAIM Million (secondary summaries of the WebAIM report); the public sector is unlikely to be better than the top million
cost_of_failure: Residents with disabilities cannot pay bills, view agendas, register to vote or find election information (DOJ found a county election website in violation of Title II); entities face DOJ findings, complaints and settlements; audit and remediation contracts run from thousands to six figures. Per-entity figures: unknown.
existing_workaround: Overlay widgets, waiting for the vendor's next CMS version, posting an accessibility statement with a phone number, pushing the deadline problem to the next budget cycle (the April 2026 extension bought a year)
who_pays_today: Public entities (taxpayers) pay audit firms, overlay vendors and CMS vendors; accessibility consultants; disability-rights organizations fund complaints

sources.note: DOJ interim final rule effective April 20, 2026 pushed Title II web deadlines to April 26, 2027 (50k+ population) and April 26, 2028 (smaller entities and special districts); obligations continue meanwhile.
DOJ small-entity guide: web content and mobile app requirements apply to all state and local governments; hiring an outside developer does not shift the duty.
Vendor guide: no small-entity or volunteer exemption; large-site remediation routinely takes 12-18 months; DOJ has not endorsed overlays.
DOJ finding that a county's election website was inaccessible to individuals with disabilities in violation of Title II.
Summary of 2026 WebAIM Million: 95.9% of home pages have detectable WCAG 2 failures (up from 94.8%), 56.1 errors per page (+10.1%).
Notes the same six failure categories (contrast, alt text, form labels, empty links/buttons, language) have topped the study for its entire duration.
State guidance for municipalities referencing the separate schedule for entities under 50,000 population.

firsthand_evidence: No firsthand complaint from a small-town webmaster was found in this session (Reddit threads did not surface in search results). The best available evidence is structural: DOJ's own small-entity guide stating there is no exemption and that outsourcing does not shift liability, plus the WebAIM failure rates.
key_unknowns: How many of the roughly 90,000 US local governments have started; what share of small-entity sites are on a handful of civic CMS vendors (which would make the problem a vendor problem, not an entity problem); whether the 2026 extension signals further delay or weaker enforcement; what small entities actually spend on audits
technical_unlock: Headless-browser crawling (Playwright) plus axe-core plus a vision-language model can produce a prioritized, plain-language remediation list per page and generate fixes (alt text, labels, contrast tokens) as pull requests or CMS edits; this was expert labor two years ago
why_now: Title II web rule deadlines are now fixed at April 2027 and April 2028; the April 2026 extension moved the panic by a year, not away; DOJ states overlays are not a path to compliance; WebAIM shows the web got worse in 2026
existing_solutions: Level Access, AudioEye, accessiBe, UsableNet, Siteimprove, Deque axe, Monsido/Acquia Optimize, civic CMS vendors (CivicPlus, Granicus), regional ADA centers, free DOJ guidance

title: People who want a private, local AI assistant cannot get local models to call tools reliably, so local agents break on real tasks
affected_user: Self-hosters, privacy-sensitive professionals and small businesses running Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or Open WebUI on their own hardware; developers building local-first agents for them
job_to_be_done: Run an agent on private data (files, email, databases, home automation) locally so nothing leaves the machine, with the same tool-use reliability they get from a cloud model
current_process: Pull an open-weight model into Ollama/LM Studio, wire it to an agent framework (opencode, Open WebUI tool servers, MCP, LangChain, smolagents) and hope the model emits well-formed tool calls; otherwise fall back to a cloud API
what_fails: Models emit malformed tool-call JSON (stray backticks, quotes, angle brackets), hallucinate tool names, pick irrelevant tools, or never call tools even though the tool server is connected; runtimes log parse failures as warnings while the client hangs and burns GPU time; fixes are per-model and per-version and regress on the next release
failure_frequency: Reported repeatedly across models and versions through 2025-2026: Ollama #15315 (Gemma 4, April 2026, dozens of comments, still reported in July 2026 by other users), #12187 (GPT-OSS not completing tool calls, Sept 2025, 41 comments), Open WebUI threads in April, May and June 2026; a Hugging Face forum user reported every local model throwing invalid-tool errors while the hosted API worked
cost_of_failure: Hours of per-model debugging (users tried Modelfile, stop-sequence, template, temperature and prompt changes without success); wasted GPU time on stuck generations; projects abandoned or routed to cloud, which defeats the privacy purpose. Dollar figures: unknown.
existing_workaround: Toggle function-calling modes back and forth (Open WebUI with Gemma 4), downgrade/upgrade runtime versions, switch to llama.cpp, add a repair proxy such as toolrails, use constrained decoding, or send the sensitive task to a cloud model anyway
who_pays_today: Users pay in hardware (GPUs) and time; companies pay cloud API bills for work they wanted to keep local; open-source maintainers absorb the triage load

sources.note: Gemma 4 tool-call parsing failures across e4b/26b/31b on Linux, macOS and LM Studio; agent clients (opencode, Copilot) hang; maintainer says small models emit malformed calls and added repair logic; others still reporting failures in July 2026.
GPT-OSS not completing tool calls; open bug with ~41 comments.
Qwen3 tool-call hallucination bug (closed).

June 2026 discussion: MCP/OpenAPI tool server reachable and lists tools but local models never trigger calls; April 2026 bug that Gemma 4 tool calls need toggling function-calling modes; MCPO servers connected but not invoked (46 comments).
User building a database agent reports local Ollama models throwing invalid-tool errors, choosing irrelevant tools or making up answers while a hosted API worked.
Third-party proxy that exists specifically to repair malformed local-model tool calls; its own description says it cannot make a weak model choose the right tool.
Native MCP support request with ~60 thumbs-up, one of the most-upvoted open Ollama issues.
Vendor commentary that local models suit well-defined agentic tasks while frontier cloud models remain more reliable for complex tool use and error recovery.

firsthand_evidence: In Ollama issue #15315 (April 2026) a user on 0.23.1 described a stuck backtick in a tool call making the process spin and consume GPU while their Copilot client waited, and asked that parser failures be surfaced as errors on the OpenAI-compatible endpoint instead of logged as warnings; another user said none of Modelfile, stop-sequence, template, temperature or prompt changes fixed the 31b model. An Open WebUI user in June 2026 reported the tool server was reachable and exposed tools but local models never actually called them.
key_unknowns: How many local-LLM users are trying agentic workflows versus plain chat; willingness to pay (this community skews toward free tools); whether the next generation of open-weight models closes the gap on its own within 6-12 months, which would erase the problem
technical_unlock: Constrained/grammar-based decoding (llguidance, GBNF) can force syntactically valid tool calls on any local model; small fine-tuned 'router' models can pick tools; runtime-level repair and validation layers can be built as an OpenAI-compatible proxy by one developer and tested with Playwright-style harnesses across models
why_now: Open-weight models with native function-calling (Gemma 4, GPT-OSS, Qwen3) shipped in 2025-2026 and MCP became the standard tool interface, so expectations jumped while reliability lagged; privacy pressure (EU AI Act, HIPAA, client confidentiality) keeps demand for local agents growing
existing_solutions: Ollama repair logic (PR #15374), toolrails, llama.cpp grammars, Outlines, LM Studio, Open WebUI native function-calling mode, Jan, LocalAI

title: Personal browser automation for everyday tasks (price checks, forms, bookings) is blocked by anti-bot systems, even when the user is acting for themselves
affected_user: Individuals and small businesses using browser agents or scripts for their own accounts and errands; developers of personal-automation tools; people with disabilities who use automation as an access aid
job_to_be_done: Have software complete a routine web task on the user's behalf (check a grocery price, fill a repetitive form, book an appointment) without being challenged, blocked or banned
current_process: Run a Playwright/CDP-driven agent (browser-use, Playwright scripts) possibly with stealth patches, residential proxies or hosted 'stealth' browsers; when blocked, solve CAPTCHAs by hand or abandon the task
what_fails: Akamai, Cloudflare and similar systems detect CDP automation markers and synthetic events and serve CAPTCHAs or error pages; stealth modes and saved profiles do not help on hardened retail sites; CAPTCHA-solving integrations raise policy and legality concerns; detection evasion is an arms race that breaks on every browser update
failure_frequency: Site-dependent but persistent: the browser-use tracker shows 61 issues matching cloudflare/captcha/bot-detection (as of this fetch), with new ones through October 2026; the Kroger issue reports every tried configuration failing
cost_of_failure: Task not completed; time spent on proxies and stealth configs; paid hosted-browser subscriptions; for disabled users, loss of an access aid. Dollar figures: unknown.
existing_workaround: Hosted stealth browsers and proxies from the automation vendor, nodriver/cloakbrowser-style undetected backends, manual CAPTCHA solving, doing the task by hand, giving up on hardened sites
who_pays_today: Users pay for hosted browser/proxy services and CAPTCHA-solving APIs; site operators pay bot-management vendors; automation vendors absorb support load

sources.note: User could not get a product price from Kroger: Akamai bot protection and CAPTCHAs blocked stealth sessions, US proxy, saved profile and the cloud playground; maintainer pointed to hosted stealth infrastructure; June 2026 comment attributes detection to Playwright CDP markers.

61 issues matching anti-bot terms, including 'Reintroduce Stealth' (closed Mar 2026), synthetic-event leak (Mar 2026), local CAPTCHA solving (Feb 2026), and Outbound Web Bot Auth signing (opened Oct 16, 2026).
Feature request for Web Bot Auth request signing, reflecting the emerging 'identified agent' standard as a way through anti-bot walls.

firsthand_evidence: A browser-use user on Windows 11 reported that the agent could not look up a single grocery item's price on Kroger because Akamai bot protection and CAPTCHAs returned error pages under every configuration tried (stealth, US proxy, saved profile, cloud playground); they stated the site's protections, not the agent or prompt, were the cause.
key_unknowns: How often ordinary people (not developers) hit this; which sites matter most for personal tasks; whether Web Bot Auth / Cloudflare's signed-agent program will legitimately admit consumer agents (which would change the problem from evasion to identity); legal exposure of evasion tooling
technical_unlock: Web Bot Auth (HTTP message signatures identifying agents) and Cloudflare's agent-identification program create a sanctioned path; a consumer-side agent that signs requests, keeps a real user profile, and falls back to a human-in-the-loop CAPTCHA step is buildable with Playwright by one developer
why_now: Browser agents went mainstream in 2025-2026 and anti-bot vendors responded; Web Bot Auth drafts and signed-agent programs appeared in 2025-2026, so there is a new legitimate mechanism to build against
existing_solutions: browser-use cloud stealth browsers, Browserbase, nodriver, cloakbrowser, undetected-chromedriver, CAPTCHA-solving APIs, Cloudflare Web Bot Auth / verified bots

title: Families are locked out of a deceased relative's photos, email and accounts because almost no one sets up legacy access, and post-death recovery requires court orders and months
affected_user: Surviving spouses, adult children and executors; older adults who hold the accounts; probate attorneys
job_to_be_done: Recover photos, documents, financial records and correspondence from a deceased person's Apple/Google/Microsoft accounts and devices, and close or transfer subscriptions and accounts
current_process: If no Legacy Contact / Inactive Account Manager was set, the family submits a death certificate and usually a court order specific enough for the platform's legal team; passcode-locked devices cannot be unlocked without erasing them; passwords/keychain are excluded even with a Legacy Contact
what_fails: The pre-planning tools exist but are unknown or unused (a 2026 Canadian interview study found only four participants had set up a legacy contact on any platform; a 2026 article cites a study finding almost none of surveyed older adults had heard of the tools); the post-death route takes months and requires lawyers; data is lost when devices are erased or accounts deleted for inactivity
failure_frequency: Every death of an account holder without pre-planning; per the awareness findings above this is the large majority. Exact share: unknown.
cost_of_failure: Irreplaceable photos and records lost; probate attorney fees and court petitions; months of delay (one guide reports families seeing timelines in months rather than weeks); recurring subscription charges continue
existing_workaround: Keep a paper list of passwords; share the phone passcode with a spouse; password-manager emergency access; hire a probate attorney; estate-planning templates; 'digital legacy' startups
who_pays_today: Families pay attorneys and court fees; estate planners sell digital-asset add-ons; platforms absorb support cost; some pay for digital-vault services

sources.note: Apple requires and verifies legal documentation for a deceased person's account and cannot remove a device passcode without erasing the device; Legacy Contact is the pre-planned route.
Legacy Contact excludes purchased media and iCloud Keychain (passwords, payment info, passkeys).
Vendor blog: without a named contact the route is a probate attorney, court petition and an order specific enough for Apple's legal team; families report months-long timelines.

GI 2026 poster (Wermie and Latulipe, Univ. of Manitoba): only four participants in the interview study had set up a legacy contact on at least one platform despite features existing on Facebook and Google.
Personal-finance piece (Nov 2, 2026) on accounts being locked at death without a legacy contact; cites a 2026 study that almost none of surveyed older adults had heard of platform legacy tools.
CHI 2026 interview study of 14 older adults on digital and material legacies (Thangaraj, Brubaker, Dixon, Pradhan).

firsthand_evidence: No direct family complaint surfaced in search results this session; the firsthand layer here is the interview studies (older adults largely unaware of or not using legacy features) and Apple's own statement that passcode-locked devices can only be erased. Treat the months-long timelines as vendor-reported.
key_unknowns: The actual distribution of recovery times and legal costs; how often platforms refuse access even with a court order; whether password-manager emergency-access features already cover the people who would pay; the size of the segment who would act in advance (the core failure is inaction)
technical_unlock: None novel on the platform side; the solvable part is the pre-planning friction (a guided, verified setup across Apple/Google/Microsoft/password manager with periodic checks) and the post-death paperwork workflow, both of which are software and forms rather than privileged access
why_now: Apple Legacy Contact and Google Inactive Account Manager now exist on every mainstream platform, so the gap is adoption rather than capability; 2026 HCI studies quantify the awareness gap; the first cohort to hold a lifetime of photos only in the cloud is now dying
existing_solutions: Apple Legacy Contact, Google Inactive Account Manager, Facebook memorialization, 1Password/Bitwarden emergency access, Everplans, Cake, Sunset (hellosunset.com), Cipherwill, estate-planning attorneys

title: Screen-reader users hit web patterns that neither the site nor the assistive technology handles, and developers cannot tell from automated tests
affected_user: Blind and low-vision people using NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver or TalkBack on web apps (banking, healthcare portals, work tools); front-end developers and small agencies who are now liable under Title II, EAA and ADA Title III litigation
job_to_be_done: Complete a multi-step web task (log in, fill a form, use a data table, dismiss a dialog) with a screen reader; for developers, ship a page that actually works with screen readers rather than one that passes a linter
current_process: Developers run axe/Lighthouse and fix flagged items; few test with a real screen reader; screen-reader users memorize workarounds, switch browsers, or call support; assistive-tech projects carry decade-old open issues for ARIA features
what_fails: Automated checks catch only the six classic errors (contrast, alt text, labels, empty links/buttons, language) and those are still on 95.9% of home pages; beyond that, ARIA relationships (aria-controls, aria-describedby on groups, aria-sort changes, flowto), dialog focus return, landmark repetition in modals and web-component clicks are unsupported or buggy in NVDA with issues open since 2014-2026, so even 'correct' markup may not work
failure_frequency: Per the 2026 WebAIM Million, 95.9% of home pages fail automated checks with 56.1 errors per page (up 10.1% year over year); unsupported-ARIA failures are not counted at all
cost_of_failure: Users excluded from services and employment tasks; ADA Title III web lawsuits continue at thousands per year (digitalapplied.com summary page, not independently verified here); EAA fines in the EU; remediation re-work after launch. Per-site figures: unknown.
existing_workaround: Users: switch screen reader/browser combos, use mobile app instead, ask sighted help. Developers: manual testing by hired screen-reader users, accessibility consultants, overlays, 'accessibility statement' disclaimers
who_pays_today: Companies pay audit firms, overlay vendors, litigation settlements; developers' time; screen-reader users' unpaid time; NV Access and vendors maintain the AT side

sources.note: Summary of the 2026 WebAIM Million: low-contrast text on 83.9% of pages, missing alt text 53.1%, missing form labels 51.0%.
Secondary summary citing WebAIM 2026: empty links 46.3%, empty buttons 30.6%.

Most-reacted open NVDA issues include aria-controls support (open since 2018), aria-describedby on groups in browse mode (2021), aria-sort changes not announced (2020), ARIA flowto (2014), dialog content read twice (2018), landmarks repeated in modals (Jan 2026), web-component click blocked in Chrome (2025).
2026 statistics and lawsuit-data roundup (content not independently verified in this session).
Commentary that AI-generated front-ends commonly fail basic accessibility checks.

firsthand_evidence: NVDA's issue tracker carries years-old, highly-reacted reports from screen-reader users and developers that standard ARIA relationships are not announced and that dialogs and landmarks are read twice; a January 2026 issue reports landmark regions announced multiple times in modal dialogs across several browsers and apps.
key_unknowns: What fraction of real task failures come from site errors versus AT gaps; whether small developers will pay for screen-reader-level testing or only for a lawsuit shield; how much 'vibe-coded' output worsens the baseline (commentary only, no measurement found)
technical_unlock: Driving a real screen reader (NVDA is open source and scriptable; macOS VoiceOver has AppleScript hooks) inside a Playwright harness and having a language model judge the spoken output against the task is now feasible, turning 'does this work with a screen reader' into an automated CI check rather than a consultant engagement
why_now: EAA enforcement began June 2025; Title II deadlines fixed for 2027-2028; WebAIM 2026 shows regression; the volume of AI-generated front-end code rose sharply in 2025-2026
existing_solutions: axe-core/Deque, Lighthouse, WAVE, Guidepup (screen-reader driver), Assistiv Labs, Evinced, Fable (user testing), Accessibility Insights, overlays

title: Adult children managing an aging parent's devices, accounts and scam exposure have no sanctioned way to do it without either taking over the identity or being locked out
affected_user: Adult children and informal caregivers of older adults; the older adults themselves; banks and platforms fielding the resulting support calls
job_to_be_done: Keep a parent's phone, email, bank and subscription accounts working and safe (password resets, 2FA codes, blocking scam calls, catching fraudulent charges) from a distance, with the parent's consent, without becoming an untraceable co-owner of their identity
current_process: Share passwords informally, hold the parent's phone during 2FA, set up family-sharing or a shared password manager, redirect mail, add call blocking, and intervene after a scam is discovered
what_fails: Platforms treat the caregiver as either the account holder (full, invisible access, which also matches the profile of elder financial abuse) or a stranger (no access); 2FA tied to a phone the parent cannot operate blocks resets; scam exposure is discovered after money is gone; nearly half of elder financial abuse is committed by someone the older adult knows, so informal full access is itself the risk vector
failure_frequency: unknown; guidance sites describe it as common but no primary statistic on caregiver-managed accounts was found this session
cost_of_failure: Scam losses (platform guidance sites describe AI voice-clone scams that get past technical defenses), hours on support lines, family conflict and legal exposure for the caregiver; dollar figures from a primary source: not found this session
existing_workaround: Password managers with emergency access, Apple/Google family features, caller-ID and number blocking, 'pause and verify' rules for money requests, powers of attorney, elder-law attorneys
who_pays_today: Families (scam losses, attorney fees), banks (fraud losses and call-center time), elder-law practices, home-care agencies that market scam-protection advice

sources.note: Elder-law guidance recommending password managers for accounts that can reset other accounts (Apple ID/Google) and 2FA; warns compromise of email or phone exposes retirement funds.
Similar guidance; notes AI-generated voice scams imitating a loved one defeat technical defenses.
Home-care vendor guidance on family-sharing monitoring and mail redirection for people with dementia.
Senior-living guidance noting that nearly half of elder financial abuse is committed by someone the older adult knows.

firsthand_evidence: No firsthand caregiver complaint was retrieved this session (the Reddit-targeted search was not executed because the shared search budget ran out). The record rests on practitioner guidance and one structural statistic, so the core claim is not yet verified.
key_unknowns: Primary statistics on caregiver-managed accounts and on scam losses attributable to this gap (FTC/FBI IC3 elder-fraud data would be the source to pull next); whether banks' existing trusted-contact and view-only features already cover the need; willingness of older adults to consent to delegated access
technical_unlock: Delegated, scoped, auditable access (view-only, approval-required actions, shared 2FA relay with logging) is a design and integration problem rather than a research problem; passkeys and platform family-sharing APIs make a consent-based delegation layer more feasible than two years ago
why_now: AI voice-clone scams targeting older adults rose in 2025-2026 per practitioner guidance; passkeys are replacing passwords, which changes how delegation would work
existing_solutions: Apple/Google family sharing, 1Password Families and emergency access, Carefull, EverSafe, bank trusted-contact programs, call-blocking apps, elder-law attorneys
